summary: Seven concrete tools and learning resources were selected from verified HN comment endorsements.
telegram_footer: 7 items surfaced | 30/30 current front-page stories processed | history + run artifact updated.

items.name: Woxi
items.source_story_title: Show HN: Woxi - Open-source Mathematica / Wolfram Language reimplementation
items.summary: An open-source Rust reimplementation of Mathematica and the Wolfram Language.
items.why_included: It received concrete positive reports for symbolic algebra and notebook compatibility from experienced CAS users.
items.evidence: One commenter tested algebra problems across several CAS tools and said Woxi was among the few to produce the expected answers.

evidence_sources.author: bobajeff
evidence_sources.excerpt: I've tried a few algebra problems with Sympy, Sage, Xcas, Maxima and Woxi. Of these only Sage, Maxima and Woxi were capable of giving the expected answers.

items.name: Shade Map
items.summary: An interactive map for visualizing terrain, building, and tree shadows by time and date.
items.why_included: It has clear practical use cases, including planning solar-panel placement and checking sight lines.
items.evidence: A commenter said it helped their group choose a solar-panel location at a wooded campsite, avoiding generator use until later.

evidence_sources.author: km3r
evidence_sources.excerpt: My friends and I used this for a camping party's solar panel's placement (for charging a battery).

items.name: F.B. Purity
items.source_story_title: uBlock Origin Is Giving Up the Fight to Keep Ads Off Facebook
items.summary: A browser extension that filters Facebook content and interface clutter.
items.why_included: It was offered as a durable practical alternative while uBlock Origin maintainers step back from Facebook-specific filters.
items.evidence: A commenter reported using it successfully across multiple browsers for years.

evidence_sources.author: The-Old-Hacker
evidence_sources.excerpt: I use a browser extension called F.B. Purity. It's worked across multiple browsers for years.

items.name: Dasher
items.summary: A predictive text-entry interface driven by next-character probabilities.
items.why_included: It is a distinctive, mature interface idea with a direct recommendation from someone familiar with its creator's work.
items.evidence: A commenter described David MacKay as a great explainer and praised Dasher as an early language-model-like text-entry tool.

evidence_sources.author: smath
evidence_sources.excerpt: Ah Sir David MacKay. I so respect him. Great explainer and speaker. He had built this text entry tool called Dasher [0]

items.name: Compression is Intelligence
items.summary: A 3Blue1Brown video exploring the relationship between compression and intelligence.
items.why_included: It is a highly praised visual explainer for a recurring thread of discussion about language models and compression.
items.evidence: A commenter explicitly called it an excellent video in an ongoing series.

evidence_sources.author: sheeeeesh
evidence_sources.excerpt: Grant Sanderson has an excellent video on the same topic [0]. It's part of a series that is ongoing.

items.name: 2026 Eclipse Webcams
items.summary: An open-source map collecting webcams along the 2026 total solar-eclipse path.
items.why_included: It is a compact, open-source utility that commenters praised for its simplicity and usefulness around a live event.
items.evidence: A commenter linked the project repository and described it as simple and elegant.

items.name: Delphi 13 Community Edition
items.source_story_title: Delphi 13 Community Edition Is Now Available
items.summary: A free community edition of the native Object Pascal development environment.
items.why_included: It remains notable for rapid visual prototyping that can grow into mature desktop software.
items.evidence: A commenter credited Delphi with enabling single developers to prototype quickly and sustain products as they gained users.

evidence_sources.author: kqr
evidence_sources.excerpt: there is (was?) something promoted by a Delphi environment that is rare to find elsewhere, that lets people (a) quickly prototype cool stuff, and then (b) sustainably grow it into a mature product as it gains users.
